rules.earth_instinct: Probably dust or a bad sensor. Wait and see.
rules.vesta_decides: Treat the alarm as an early-phase fire. Warn, gather, send the alert.
rules.limits: A design statement from the SAME fact sheet about what detection must target; it did not test this vehicle's detector.
rules.nasa_showed: Given the constrained space on any spacecraft, the target for the fire detection system is necessarily the early phase and not established flaming fires; consequently, the primary target for detection is pyrolysis products rather than soot.

rules.vesta_decides: Stop forced airflow to the module.
rules.limits: Review statements about microgravity experiments in general; no oxygen level is stated and this cabin is at 34 %.
rules.nasa_showed: Microgravity experiments demonstrated that the assumed margin of safety of reduced flammability in microgravity, based on quiescent test results, may not be valid for most spacecraft environments where ventilation flow strongly enhances flames.

rules.vesta_decides: Do not use an upward flame shape to locate a low-momentum fire in microgravity.
rules.limits: A description of low-momentum flames on the station, not a panel-search procedure. Jets and pressurised leaks can behave differently; follow the separately cited ISS mask and investigation procedure only within its vehicle limits.
rules.nasa_showed: In microgravity, this flow doesn't occur and on the space station, low-momentum flames tend to be rounded or even spherical.

rules.vesta_decides: Remove power from the zone before discharging anything.
rules.nasa_showed: crew will proceed to unpower the equipment behind the panel, thus attacking the Ignition Source (Heat) leg of the fire triangle.

rules.earth_instinct: Aim at the base of the flame.
rules.vesta_decides: Do not assume a close jet will extinguish the flame.
rules.limits: BASS burned small solid samples in a flow duct. The quotes show that a local jet can fail; they do not show that flooding works. No oxygen level is stated.
rules.nasa_showed: Also, current findings show that local application of suppressant is not adequate for flame extinguishment. The local jet entrains air and sustains the flame even when the ambient airflow is turned off.

rules.vesta_decides: Masks stay on. Keep sampling combustion products until the readings are clear.
rules.limits: Cool flames were seen on liquid fuel droplets (FLEX). This fire is solid or electrical: a different fuel class.
rules.nasa_showed: FLEX, which analyzed the effectiveness of fire suppressants, led to the discovery of a type of cool flame, where the fuel continued "burning" under certain conditions after extinction of the visible flame.

rules.earth_instinct: If it passed the flammability test on Earth, it is fine in space.
rules.vesta_decides: Treat Earth test margins as unproven for this cabin: check the material on the Design map.
rules.limits: The sentences state no oxygen level; the cabin's oxygen may lie outside every solid test in the base.
rules.nasa_showed: Recent results from the BASS experiment currently running on the ISS indicate that NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 is not conservative, and materials can burn at lower oxygen levels in microgravity than on Earth.

rules.earth_instinct: The visible flame is gone, so combustion has stopped.
rules.vesta_decides: Keep visible-flame extinction separate from confirmation that combustion has stopped.
rules.limits: FLEX observed cool flames in liquid fuel droplets under certain conditions. This does not establish cool-flame burning in a solid or electrical cabin fire, or a sensor clearance threshold.
rules.nasa_showed: FLEX, which analyzed the effectiveness of fire suppressants, led to the discovery of a type of cool flame, where the fuel continued "burning" under certain conditions after extinction of the visible flame.

rules.earth_instinct: Any inert gas will affect a flame the same way.
rules.vesta_decides: Keep the tested diluent in the evidence match; do not substitute one inert gas for another.
rules.limits: ISS liquid-droplet results compare cool-flame extinction diameters and burning duration for particular gas mixtures. They do not establish a whole-cabin suppression dose or crew-safe atmosphere.
rules.nasa_showed: Different diluents were observed to exert remarkably different influences on the cool-flame combustion of fuel droplets.

rules.earth_instinct: Once helium kills the hot flame, burning ends immediately.
rules.vesta_decides: Allow for a brief cool-flame stage after hot-flame extinction in this helium-diluted droplet test.
rules.limits: Test R707 used an n-octane droplet with 75% helium dilution. The authors call the process transient, not quasi-steady. This is not a helium discharge instruction for an occupied cabin.
rules.nasa_showed: The hot flame that formed during the ignition dies within a fraction of a second and the cool flame burning commences immediately which also ends quickly leaving the droplet to evaporate.

rules.earth_instinct: A familiar material will burn the same way in richer oxygen.
rules.vesta_decides: Treat elevated oxygen as a change in fire conditions, rather than carrying over an air result.
rules.limits: The quoted Saffire-V result describes more energetic flames at elevated oxygen. It does not quantify a universal increase, cover all materials, or certify a cabin atmosphere.
rules.nasa_showed: The elevated oxygen levels show more energetic flames, which would have a larger impact on the vehicle

rules.earth_instinct: The same fuel and airflow make enclosure size irrelevant.
rules.vesta_decides: Keep the flow-duct geometry with the flame-spread result when comparing designs.
rules.limits: The reduced-height Saffire flow duct increased SIBAL spread rate relative to Saffire I and III. The reported increase belongs to that comparison, not every cabin or material.
rules.nasa_showed: As expected, the spread rate increased (about 100%) with the reduced height flow duct compared to Saffire I and III.

rules.earth_instinct: One smoke-detector technology catches every kind of smoke equally.
rules.vesta_decides: Check detector response against the smoke particles the material produces.
rules.limits: SAME produced sub-micron particles from its tested samples. The quote also says light scattering performed very well in most cases. It does not select or validate a detector for this vehicle.
rules.nasa_showed: All samples produced significant numbers of sub-micron particulate that are better detected using an ionization smoke detector, however a light scattering detector would perform very well for most of the cases.

rules.earth_instinct: Airflow always carries a flame downstream.
rules.vesta_decides: Include upstream spread when considering the low-flow space result.
rules.limits: The BASS observation applies at low forced-flow velocities in space. The quote supplies no universal velocity threshold and does not describe every fuel, geometry or gravity level.
rules.nasa_showed: Completely contrary to normal-gravity behavior, the flame spreads upstream, into the oncoming airflow, in space when the forced-flow velocities are low

rules.earth_instinct: Once the flame disappears, the solid stops supplying fuel.
rules.vesta_decides: Account for continued vapor release while hot PMMA cools after extinction.
rules.limits: The reported PMMA rod behavior concerns concurrent-flow geometry in microgravity. It does not supply a cooldown time, an air-clearance threshold or a procedure for every cabin material.
rules.nasa_showed: After extinction, the hot material can continue to produce fuel for some time until it cools.
